slides: Welcome back, and now the circle chart. It comes up quite a lot on the exam.
It looks different from everything we've seen. But we'll see that it's an old friend.

slides.say: We know the story already. It's the visitors on the Psycho website, over twenty-four hours.
The hours go round the circle, like a clock. Zero at the top.
at: The hours go round the circle

slides.say: The number of visitors is shown by the circles. A hundred, two hundred, up to five hundred on the big circle.
The dark rings outside show where most of the visitors are in each hour. They're the strips from the last chart, bent round the circle.

slides: From the outside in, the rings are explanations, practice, forum, and other.

slides.say: The example says, at nine o'clock there were three hundred visitors. And between nine and ten, most of them were in the forum.
Let's find nine o'clock on the clock. We go in along that line, to the teal curve. It's on the circle of three hundred.
at: We go in along that line

slides.say: And between nine and ten, the dark part is in the third ring. The third ring is the forum. It matches.
Notice, every chart we've seen so far, except the table, was on axes. Here the axes are just bent into a circle.
So the circle chart can have points, like points on axes. Or bars, each bar going out to its value.
Or one continuous line, like here.
Here's the continuous chart from the last lesson, next to the circle chart. They show exactly the same data.
At twelve o'clock, the continuous line is a bit above three hundred. About three hundred twenty.
In the circle, at twelve, the curve is also just past the three hundred circle.
And from twelve to sixteen, most visitors were in the explanations. Below the chart it's the explanations strip. In the circle it's the outer ring.
Now a sample question. What is the latest hour at which there are visitors in the practice area?
The practice ring is the second one. Going round, its last dark part ends at twenty o'clock.
So is the answer twenty o'clock? A lot of students mark it. But let's read what the dark areas mean.
They show where most of the visitors are in that hour. Most, not all.
What does most mean? More than half. Say there are three hundred visitors, and a hundred sixty are in the forum. That's most of them.

slides: The other hundred forty can be anywhere, also in the practice area. So after twenty o'clock, some people may still practise. Or maybe nobody does.

slides.say: The chart can't tell us. So the latest hour cannot be known.
So the circle chart is just a chart on axes. The circles are the lines of the value axis, bent round.
We could cut the circle open at the top and unfold it. Then we'd get the same chart on straight axes.
